decision: each writer probes its pinned file every 2 s and treats link count 0, a missing path or another inode as lost; ESTALE and EIO do not count

evidence: a_store_unlinked_under_its_runtime_closes_its_files_and_reopens_fresh; disabling the probe leaves the store healthy

decision: the lost attachment drops its reader pool at once and the registry drops the runtime without waiting for reader workers
why: the spec requires no descriptor into the deleted files within one probe interval; retaining the pool to wait for it keeps the pool's pinned descriptor open
evidence: review finding 2 and 4; the pool's pinned file lives in its shared state until the last reader lease drops
result: follow-up: release that descriptor on loss, then retain the pool until it quiesces

decision: attachment drain releases its state lock before joining the writer and serializes concurrent drains with a separate gate
why: the writer's lost-file notice takes the state lock, so a drain that joined while holding it deadlocked when the probe was due during shutdown
result: drain returns while the writer finishes

decision: evicting a lost runtime also clears the profile pins recorded on its key
why: stale pins on a reopened key counted against the fresh runtime's shutdown hold
result: pins on the dead runtime are gone

decision: ProfileLost ends the daemon with exit status 66 after the ordinary graceful shutdown, not 0
why: the launchd unit restarts only after a failed exit (SuccessfulExit=false); systemd restarts on any exit; changing the plist would also restart intentional stops
evidence: deleting_the_profile_under_a_running_daemon_ends_it_as_profile_lost asserts the status; it saw 0 before the change

decision: closing a lost file closes the reader pool's pinned descriptor itself, for every holder, instead of dropping the pool
why: a reader lease or retained snapshot holds the pool object, so dropping the attachment's handle left the unlinked inode open until the last lease ended
evidence: a_lost_file_closes_every_descriptor_while_a_reader_pool_is_still_held fails without close_for_lost_file and without the descriptor release
result: descriptor closed on loss; pool object may outlive it

decision: a worker registered after the lost-file sweep is shut down at registration
why: a growing acquire that spawned before the close inserts its worker after the sweep and it idled until the pool dropped
result: no idle worker survives a lost file

decision: a lost runtime stays mapped as Evicting until its reader workers exit; lookup answers Evicting and open is refused with RuntimeEvictionInProgress for that short window
why: publishing a successor beside readers still open on the old file; close_exact_stale_attachment needs write-scope authority, refuses a leased runtime and is async, so it cannot run from the synchronous lookup
result: a caller that opens inside the window gets a typed retryable refusal; no retry added

decision: lost_file_closed also requires the lost writer task to have finished; the attachment keeps the lost writer in a lost slot and moves readers and writer there in the same lock hold that marks the file lost
why: the writer connection closes only when its task returns after the notice, so the registry could unmap and reopen the key beside a still-open writer; a separate lock for the move left a window where nothing was left to wait on
result: the Evicting window now spans the writer task exit too

decision: a reader acquire that finds the pool draining because of a lost file reports FileLost, and close_for_lost_file flips draining and lost under one lock
why: the rest of the lost path reports FileLost and a blocked caller would otherwise see a retryable-looking Draining; setting the two under separate locks let a woken waiter see Draining without lost
evidence: an_acquire_blocked_when_the_file_is_lost_reports_file_lost and a_worker_spawned_while_the_pool_closes_for_a_lost_file_exits fail without the FileLost reason
result: waiters and later acquires get FileLost
